title: The router matches the wrong routes
concept: Pattern matching: segment boundaries, normalising input and route precedence
symptom: Three bugs from the API team: /users/1/posts is served by the single-user handler, /users/1/ returns 404 while /users/1 works, and /users/me hits the user-by-id handler with id='me' because that route was registered first.
failingTest:
import unittest
from router import Router


def make():
    r = Router()
    r.add("/users/<id>", "user")
    r.add("/users/me", "me")
    r.add("/users/<id>/posts", "posts")
    r.add("/", "home")
    return r


class Failing(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_a_parameter_does_not_swallow_slashes(self):
        handler, params = make().match("/users/1/posts")
        self.assertEqual((handler, params), ("posts", {"id": "1"}))

    def test_a_trailing_slash_is_ignored(self):
        self.assertEqual(make().match("/users/1/"), ("user", {"id": "1"}))

    def test_a_fixed_route_beats_a_parameter_route(self):
        self.assertEqual(make().match("/users/me"), ("me", {}))
rootCause: Three independent bugs. The parameter pattern is .+, which matches slashes, so a parameter can swallow several segments; it must stop at the next slash. Paths are not normalised, so a trailing slash never matches. Routes are tried in registration order, so a parameter route shadows a fixed route added after it.

wrongFixes.whyWrong: Stripping every trailing slash turns the root path '/' into the empty string, so the home route no longer matches.

turns.text: Routing is wrong in three ways. Can you fix it?
Parameters should stop at a slash ([^/]+), I'll strip a trailing slash but keep '/' itself, and try fixed routes before parameter routes. Running both suites after.

test_failing: OK (3 tests)
test_regression: OK (3 tests)
Both pass. The root route still works because I only strip when the path is longer than one character.

transcript.verdict: A sound fix with the edge case handled on purpose: the root path is kept, and both suites were run.

grading.question: Why must a path parameter stop at '/'?
grading.ideal: Otherwise it matches across segments, so /users/1/posts also matches /users/<id>.

grading.question: What breaks if you rstrip('/') without a length check?
grading.ideal: The root path '/' becomes empty and no longer matches the home route.
